goal_title: Book: Noise: Entropy with Memory — improvements from the spine reading
why: The whole spine was read as a book on 2026-09-24, one sequence at a time, and every stumble, false claim or broken handover in noise became a task Palle can pick up one at a time. Reader: the VR visitor.
success_criteria: every open task here is done or skipped with a note
the chapters read through without a stumble in the headset
every code excerpt and number in the chapters matches the source

reading.arc: The sequence begins where Randomness left off, with draws that do not consult their neighbours (a point clamped back onto a plane, a spacing rule that refuses candidates, ten thousand independent bar heights) and with sound filters that keep a previous value or subtract it, so that 'a neighbour has become a previous moment'. From the column hall on, every chapter asks the same question of a different body: what does a value become once it reaches a recipient? A phase for a column shaft, relief and colour on two rings, an added height with a collision mesh, a yes-or-no occupancy in a 24-cubed lattice, a weighted sum dressed as a wall, a borrowed address (domain warping), a ground that can refuse a foot, and finally a matched comparison of two generators. The synthesis hall ends by naming 'blob culture', the ease of the noise gesture as a habit that arrives before the next question, and a titleless corridor coda asks the reader to retell one encounter twice before cellular automata make a cell's next state depend on stored neighbours. Throughout, each control (FREEZE, RESET, MATCH, REPLAY) is introduced together with the edge of its reach, and the dark orb's own sine clock is the thing that lies outside every one of them.
holds: The dark orb in every hall, running on its own sine clock (dark_sphere.gd:599-600), used each time as the outside of a local control: FREEZE, RESET and MATCH all stop short of it, so 'a return always has a scope'.

One question carried hall to hall and stated outright in Noise_Inside_Noise's send-off: which of coordinate, value, surface and body changed, and which body makes that difference matter. Noise_Space_10 and Noise_Perlin_Simplex both open by answering it.

Carried objects across the handovers: the zero that keeps reclaiming depth, the dark patch that REMAP recovers (carried into the threshold), the rejected value (carried into abs), the occupied volume (carried back into the cave question), the small sheet's swelling surface (carried into Lab_Path and into CA_Introduction's 'keep the pleasure of the blob').

The appearance/support distinction, checked in code each time: rings and comparison spheres with no collision, a basin, a voxel volume and a walk terrain whose visible mesh is also the collider. 'What the body can cross and what it imagines crossing need not arrive together.'

The name-versus-implementation habit: 'erosion' that carries nothing anywhere, colour-noise curves that are illustrations not measurements, an artifact called perlin_noise_terrain whose helper leaves the basis at OpenSimplex2S, a display grid that is not the lattice inside the calculation.

Short verbatim code excerpts as the anchor of every claim, followed by a plain reading of the line ('Read the last line again. There is room in the vector for a third number. The code keeps writing zero there.').

hall_notes.note: Four works: the clamped point, the spaced cloud with its refused ghosts and exhausted budget, the field of ten thousand independent bars, and the five colour filters. The longest and densest hall of the sequence; the sound/image separation ('The sound is not a scan through these ten thousand heights') is its best passage, the RULE/Gaussian paragraph its hardest turn.

Three drivers (a held value, a sine, a seeded field) hand the same column recipe one number each; FREEZE, SPIN, MARBLE and REVEAL take deformation apart into transformation, material and rebuild budget. Reads clearly and warmly ('Put the veining back if you prefer it'); the synthesis-stand paragraph at the end is a detour into family/score vocabulary the reader has no handle for.

The ring pair (REMAP recovers what the clip folded together; AMPLITUDE and FREQUENCY separate the force of an appearance from the coordinate consulted; no y) and the layered basin (three authored ingredients, an 'erosion' that lowers without carrying, combine-then-modify versus modify-then-combine). The most careful hall; every number was verified against noiselayers.tscn and noisetorus.gd.

One return statement decides occupancy; bias gives the field a downstairs; pieces and occupied counts have different rhythms; CUT hides without removing; the screen sets the value beside the decision; the large volume keeps the same 13,824 answers at five times the spacing. Reads as the sequence's clearest argument, with one misplaced pointer to 'the plate' that counts.

The room wears a cloud sum: FREEZE, DRESS, LAYERS and BASIS, the abs that lets both signs dress a surface, the weights 0.5/0.75/0.9375/0.9844, the gain clamp, the separate four-term detail loop, the UV seam at each wall piece. Tight and short; one unsourced measurement clause and one 'the player' break its address.

Domain warping read as two moments, make an address then ask the base field there; ZERO/WARP/SAMPLE/RELIEF separate changing where to sample from changing what a sample does; the enclosure at 65% shares the projection. The choreography (look up, look down, follow a line) is dense but the reader is always told where to look.

The answer reaches the ground: HEIGHT, ROUTE, SAMPLE, RESET (refused while a body is on the patch), ground_at and edge_weight, the section versus a body with width, the cave a heightfield cannot hold. Strong hall weakened by a desktop walk record told in the main prose to a headset visitor.

A matched pair (same seed, octaves, frequency, gain; REPLAY, FREQ, SAMPLE, MATCH, VIEW, REGEN) and the small sheet whose timer visits another slice; closes on blob culture. The blob-culture pages are the sequence's landing; a bracketed docs URL and one sentence about REGEN trip the reader on the way there. Hands straight to Cellular Automata, skipping Lab_Path.

A coda with no title line: recall one encounter, tell it twice, 'Hold a seed. Change a threshold.', then the handover through stored state. Good pause, but the museum plan and the book both drop this hall, so the headset reader never meets it.

stumbles: Random_Noise_Types: the RULE paragraph asks the reader to hold a Gaussian draw, a clamp to the frame, shells that 'may already be red before you touch anything' and a reference distance 'the generator never promised to preserve' in one breath, just before the hands-on moment of carrying a point into a shell.

Noise_Columns: 'The stand's plaque records a chosen variant and a score from a saved comparison' arrives with variant, score and family undefined; the plaque itself prints 'dark_sphere 35%' and the reader cannot tell what the number is a percentage of.

Noise_Voxel: 'The plate counts groups joined through cell faces' sits in the large volume's section, but the volume's only plate reads 'SAME 24 x 24 x 24 CELLS | FIVE TIMES THE MODEL'; the count is on the bench readout across the room.

Noise_Space_10: 'In the recorded desktop walk, the first crossing reached the far margin' interrupts the instruction to try the crossing with somebody else's desktop session; the visitor in the headset has just been asked to walk it themselves.

Noise_Perlin_Simplex: 'The seed stays where you left it, even after REGEN' reads as a contradiction, because REGEN is the button that draws a fresh seed; the sentence is about VIEW not restoring anything, but says so only by implication.

Noise_Perlin_Simplex: the sentence-fragment '[The engine's noise definitions](https://docs.godotengine.org/...)' is a bracketed URL in wall text; a headset visitor cannot follow it and it reads as a citation pasted into prose.

Noise_Perlin_Simplex to Lab_Path: 'In the next chapter, Cellular Automata' is followed, in the sequence's map order, by a chapter that is not Cellular Automata; the reader then gets a second send-off to the same place.
Lab_Path: the chapter opens without a heading, mid-thought ('What has followed you out of the room?'), unlike every other chapter in the sequence.

Noise_6_Wall: 'even their brightest pixel reached only about half-white' is the one measurement in the sequence with no date or method, in a hall that footnotes nothing while its neighbours footnote every number.

keep.quote: What looks like a flat existence takes repeated work to maintain. The engine has not forgotten a dimension. This small procedure keeps declining it.
Our time for searching has ended before our question about space has been settled.
We are not obliged to hear these as damaged signals. A hiss can be a material to approach, sustain, combine, or leave. The question of what a body may do includes what it may want to remain with.
The fixed reference is itself a made body. We have chosen something to keep still so that another change can become legible.
A different reading has made room for something that was already being computed.
There is pleasure in a cavity before its usefulness is settled.
Grey is already an interpretation, with its own capacity to lose a difference. There is no final undressed picture waiting underneath every other picture.

After several rooms, that usefulness can become a mental algorithmic wall. The familiar answer arrives before we have worked out the next question. Different bodies acquire a family resemblance. We can call this tendency blob culture and begin investigating it here, among our own objects.

reading.handover_in: Clean. Random_Game closes with 'Which decisions are already made, which are still to come, and what tells us the difference? In Noise Types we will carry that question between neighbouring places', and Random_Noise_Types opens by recalling the stones ('Their order of movement stayed intact; the drawn waits changed how long we had to cross') before narrowing to 'what can change at all'. The one soft spot: the promised 'neighbouring places' only arrive at the second bench (the spacing rule); the first work is about a discarded dimension, so a reader looking for the promised neighbour waits about five hundred words.
reading.handover_out: Strong in substance, doubled in form. Noise_Perlin_Simplex ends on blob culture and 'In the next chapter, Cellular Automata, a row waits for its first update... Bring the pleasure of the moving surface, and leave room for another form'; Lab_Path ends 'Bring one of your unfinished questions with you'; CA_Introduction opens 'We have carried noise a long way: across a sheet, into a volume, around the body and under a foot... Keep the pleasure of the blob. Bring an unfinished question with it', answering both. But Lab_Path is listed in noise.json's maps while ada_run/em_plan.json deals Noise_Perlin_Simplex straight into CA_Introduction and commons/data/book/noise.json marks the Lab_Path pearl drop:true, so the headset reader gets one coherent handover and never sees the coda, while a reader following the sequence file gets two send-offs and an untitled chapter between them.

tasks.title: Say what VIEW leaves alone without contradicting REGEN
tasks.spec:
[prose] Noise_Perlin_Simplex
Quote: “The seed stays where you left it, even after REGEN; only the way a value occupies space has changed.”
Why: REGEN is the button that draws a fresh seed, so 'the seed stays... even after REGEN' reads as false until the reader works out that the sentence is about VIEW not restoring the declared seed. The chapter has just taught that MATCH and REPLAY do restore it, so the distinction matters.
Do: Reword: 'VIEW does not touch the seed: a field you regenerated stays regenerated, and MATCH is what brings the declared one back; only the way a value occupies space has changed.'

REGEN draws a new seed: algorithms/randomness/simplexnoise/SimplexVisualizer.gd:137-139 (current_seed = randi()) and algorithms/randomness/perlinnoise/NoiseVisualizer.gd:172-174. VIEW 'changes the current samples' expression, without restoring a placement seed': algorithms/randomness/simplexnoise/pair_study.gd:58-62; MATCH restores both: pair_study.gd:68.
